title: Tenant behavior probing and hotspot isolation log
summary: Evening oncall log: progressive degradation in a regional dedicated GPU pool. Short-term mitigations, hypotheses, and next steps.
content:
Context:
Evening shift (US-WEST-2). Dedicated GPU pool 'dc-west-02-pool-a' saw a gradual increase in tail latency and request timeouts starting ~18:20 PDT, culminating in a visible drop in effective throughput by 18:42. Customer impact: intermittent 503s for Dedicated tenants — mostly mid-sized batch workloads. No global outage but SLA alerts triggered for three customers on reserved capacity.

Detection signals observed:
- Console alerts: per-pool 95th latency > 2.5s for > 5m (alert rule latency-pool-95p-exceed)
- Token processing backlog increased from 200->1.2k in 15 minutes (queue depth metric)
- GPU utilization skew: 2 GPUs at 95-99% busy, 6 GPUs idle under 10% (per-host/utilization histogram)
- KV cache miss rate for affected model rose from 4% -> 28% (unexpected cache thrash)
- Allocator logged repeated "evicting-tenant" events for same tenant id (t-4487) — suspicious

Immediate actions taken (chronological):
- 18:23: Page acknowledged (oncall = Maya). Started live capture: perf counters, dmesg, driver logs.
- 18:26: Isolated kth rotational host (host-gpu-07) from load-balancer. Observed queued requests draining with no improvement in overall pool.
- 18:31: Ran tenant listing for active sessions: `tenantctl sessions --pool dc-west-02-pool-a` -> found tenant t-4487 with sustained high concurrency (200 concurrent connections) and long seq length requests.
- 18:34: Issued soft-evict for tenant t-4487 (graceful eviction) to move its sessions to burst pool: `allocator evict --tenant t-4487 --graceful`.
- 18:36: Autoscaler reported failing scale-up attempts due to insufficient slot fragmentation — saw 'insufficient-affinity' errors in allocator logs.
- 18:41: Temporarily increase pool burst capacity by toggling feature flag `burst-allow-temporary` -> +2 GPUs for 12m window. Immediate drop in latency to baseline (95p -> 1.2s) but KV miss stayed elevated.

Sleuth notes (what we inspected):
- Kernel / driver: checked dmesg on host-gpu-07 and host-gpu-08. Found repeated NVLINK PCIe warnings on host-gpu-07 (rate limited). No OOMs.
- Model behavior: affected sessions were running long autoregressive streams with many short discrete calls (prefix-heavy), causing KV cache to be reloaded per call.
- Allocation pattern: tenant t-4487 had affinity pinned to two hosts due to previous placement constraints (placement history shows affinity: gpu-type=A100-40GB, region pinned). That created a hotspot.
- Autoscaler logs: increase requests queued but rejected because node candidates failed placement checks (label mismatch for newly provisioned nodes). Root cause: new node image lacked label `gpu.kubernetes.io/kv-opt-in=true` after recent image rotation.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Noisy tenant with extreme concurrency + long streaming is thrashing per-host KV cache and saturating the few pinned GPUs (most likely).
2) Autoscaler misconfig (label drift) prevented rapid scale-up, prolonging hotspot duration.
3) Driver-level NIC/PCIe warnings amplified latency on affected host (contributor, less likely primary).

Mitigations applied and observations:
- Tenant eviction succeeded; t-4487 traffic redistributed over burst pool and other pools. Throughput recovered after ~6m.
- Temporary burst capacity allowed breathing room while we validated autoscaler config.
- Manual taint/label fix applied to node-image job: added missing label and triggered a new node provision; subsequent scale-up attempts succeeded in test stage after image repush.

Post-incident actions (short-term):
- Patch autoscaler config: add an automagic label-sanity-check preflight (JIRA-TASK-4201).
- Add a targeted alert: 'allocator-placement-rejection-rate' to detect label/constraint rejections earlier.
- Create a tenant-level concurrency limiter for Dedicated pools: soft limit 150 concurrent upstream connections; implement throttling path and graceful queuing (PR referenced above).

Longer-term follow-ups / runbook draft items:
- Runbook section: "Hotspot detection and emergency redistribution" (to be added under dedicated-pool runbooks). Steps: identify skewed utilization -> check tenant affinity -> attempt graceful eviction -> enable burst -> fix autoscaler if scale-up rejected -> escalate to infra if driver/kernel warnings present.
- Scheduled experiment: synthetic workload to simulate prefix-heavy tiny calls to measure KV miss amplification and eviction thresholds. (Owner: Ravi, target: 2025-11-10)
- Improve placement telemetry: log the actual label set used by node candidates in scale attempts.
- Add chaos test that simulates node image label drift during CI (to surface future regressions).

Notes-to-self / unresolved / open questions:
- Why did KV miss remain elevated after eviction? Could be cache re-init latency on rebalanced nodes OR application-level repeated short-lived model contexts. Need heap/profile of server process to see cache warmup timeline.
- Confirm whether NVLINK/PCIe warnings correlate with host throttling. Query kernel team for interpretation of repeated rate-limited NVML warnings.
- Should we backfill tenant history to identify other tenants with similar request patterns? We probably need a weekly job to flag tenants with >X% of long-short-call ratio.

Commands used (for traceability):
- `kubectl logs -n allocator allocator-7f9d --since=30m | grep placement | tail -n 200`
- `allocator metrics --pool dc-west-02-pool-a --window 15m | jq '.utilization_by_host'`
- `tenantctl sessions --pool dc-west-02-pool-a --tenant t-4487 --json`

Final state and customer impact summary:
- Incident start: 2025-11-03 18:20 PDT. Major mitigation (evict + burst) applied by 18:36. Latency back to baseline by 18:48. No long-term customer data loss. Affected customers saw transient 503s for up to ~8 minutes.
- Root causes: noisy tenant + autoscaler label drift. Driver warnings noted as a possible contributing factor; requires hardware team signoff.

Actions created (with owners):
- JIRA-TASK-4201: autoscaler preflight label check (Owner: Samir)
- JIRA-ENG-4220: tenant concurrency limiter design doc + API (Owner: Ravi)
- JIRA-ENG-4221: KV cache warmup profiling + measurement harness (Owner: Ellen)
- JIRA-OPS-4230: kernel/driver warning triage with infra/hardware team (Owner: Maya)

Appendix (raw snippets):
- allocator placement rejection excerpt: `placement-reject reason=label-mismatch required=gpu.kubernetes.io/kv-opt-in=true candidate=host-gpu-12` (seen 42 times between 18:20-18:36)
- dmesg snippet (host-gpu-07): `[Nov 3 18:19:52] nvlink: pcie timeout, resetting link (rate-limited)`

Quick wins to implement in next week:
- alert on placement-rejection spike (owner: Samir)
- add a guardrail in console to show per-tenant concurrency so SRE can triage faster (owner: product-console)
- short-lived: bump default soft concurrency for Dedicated to reduce immediate evictions while we ship proper limiter (owner: infra)

If anything here is unclear, ping me in #sre-dedicated and I'll paste logs. Saving this as the evening oncall capture; will convert to a formal postmortem if any customer follows up or if JIRA-INC-3124 escalation is raised.

---
Drafted by Maya Chen (oncall), verified logs w/ Ravi and Ellen.
